answer: A ferrous deposit gate stays anchored to each claimed slot: an identity must lock 20,000 POA into the slot's escrow before its attestation can wander past the local shard. If a duplicate slot owner is proven, the losing claim's ferrous lock is slashed in half and the half is paid to the counter-claimant as anchor proof of loss, while the wander-time of both claims resets to zero. Each forged identity therefore burns 10,000 POA upfront and risks the full half-slash per duplicate, so spoofing scales linearly in cost per fake slot.
